documents.text: ### Step 5: Double check your submission With your code ready to go, this is a good time to double-check your submission to make sure it follows our conventions. Here are the things to check: - The commit message is properly formatted. - The change introduces no functional regression. Be sure to run `npm test` to verify your changes before submitting a pull request. - Make separate pull requests for unrelated changes. Large pull requests with multiple unrelated changes may be closed without merging. - All changes must be accompanied by tests, even if the feature you're working on previously had no tests. - All user-facing changes must be accompanied by appropriate documentation. - Follow the [Code Conventions](./code-conventions).

request.instructions: The documents are sections of the documentation of ONE open-source project at one commit. Report a conflict only when two sections make incompatible statements about the SAME option, flag, default value, limit, version requirement, or behavior, for the same product version and scope. These are NOT conflicts: values of different options; example values in code samples that merely override a default; statements explicitly scoped to an older version or to migration history; one section giving more detail than the other; different defaults that the text ties to different contexts (per-route vs global, dev vs build, agent mode vs server mode).

a.quote: Be sure to run `npm test` to verify your changes before submitting a pull request.

b.quote: You should be sure to run `npm test` before submitting a pull request.
